### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via buildSession (symbol, a top-level function), explainAccessForCaller (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5eb0f51c0009e4e4062fa6d4118a427d917c03bc` — the merge of head `d9e058c05488a76d8aa368b66bbfbf0ad637d855` into base `09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5eb0f51c0009e4e4062fa6d4118a427d917c03bc && git checkout 5eb0f51c0009e4e4062fa6d4118a427d917c03bc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a d9e058c05488a76d8aa368b66bbfbf0ad637d855 && git checkout -B drift-repro 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a && git merge --no-ff d9e058c05488a76d8aa368b66bbfbf0ad637d855

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#4 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP8JJo4zF2sjTBRwnX

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d9e058c05488a76d8aa368b66bbfbf0ad637d855`
Local-runs: none

Declaration face, owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line. Read: card #31740 body and every comment (claim 6755718157, amendment 6755781269, triage 6730398547 and 6754783778, dev report 6756739373), the Step 0 file, the PR body, the net diff against merge base `60f8149e` (11 files, +335/-1), the head's check-runs, and ADR-0151 D5 / O4. Code outside the diff was read to check the claims, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The new key.** `HookContextSchema.session.principalKind` in `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` is `z.enum(['human','agent','service','guest','system']).optional()`. This is the same name and the same five values as `ExecutionContext.principalKind` (`kernel/execution-context.zod.ts:203`) and `ExplainDecision.principal.principalKind` (`security/explain.zod.ts:372`). The `.describe()` and the JSDoc both say it is descriptive only and not an authorization input, in the same terms used for `positions`. They also explain how to tell the two kinds of agent apart (`provenance.performedByClientId` is present or absent), and that an absent key is never defaulted. The seat's ruling (amendment 6755781269) is met.
- **Exported and published.** `HookContext` is inferred from the exported `HookContextSchema`, and the spec test reads the key through `NonNullable of HookContext['session']`. The session object is not `.strict()`, so the test shows the key is now declared rather than stripped, and that a sixth value fails at `['session','principalKind']`. The regenerated `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx` carries the same description word for word. No other generated surface mirrors the session keys (searched at head). `authorable-surface` tracks only the top-level `HookContext:session`, so no baseline moves, and `Spec property liveness` is green.
- **Other public surfaces.** None moved. The explain change has no spec change, because `ExplainDecision.principal.principalKind` already existed. The exported `buildContextForUser` is untouched. The audit writers `audit-writers.ts`, `action-invocation-audit.ts` and `data-export-audit.ts` are unchanged and only pinned.
- **ADR-0151 D5 refusals are honored.** There is no `performedBy` naming the account: the account's `assembleExecutionContext` output carries none, and the pins assert no `performed_by` and no `on_behalf_of` on the CRUD, action and export rows. There is no audit kind column: the pins assert that no `principal` or `kind` key exists on the ledger row and that `metadata` is null. There is no per-write key id: nothing in the diff records one.
- **Correctness hazards.**
  - (a) Holds. `buildSession` returns `undefined` for no `execCtx`. It copies `execCtx.principalKind` only after the all-undefined presence test, in the same place as `locale`, and it never writes `'human'`. Pins: "kind alone ⇒ undefined", "no kind ⇒ no key", and the five values copied verbatim. Ablations A1 and A2 went red, per the PR.
  - (b) Holds. The kind is stamped by `assemble-execution-context.ts:360` (`agent || account ? 'agent' : anonymous ? 'guest' : 'human'`). That assembler is reached by `resolveRequestExecutionContext` (REST, runtime dispatcher, endpoint executor), by `mcp/src/plugin.ts`, by `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` and by `print-routes.ts`. The tests build envelopes through the real assembler, not with a hand-set kind. In derived contexts (`seedUserGrants`), a person carries no key, which the describe text states as "absent ⇒ envelope reads human". An account keeps `'agent'` there (`engine-scoped-context.ts:149`), which is the direction O2 and O6 need.
  - (c) Holds. The stamp is in the `?userId=` other-user branch only, after `readSysUserRow` has asserted that the row exists, and it is guarded by `explained.principalKind === undefined`, so it never overwrites `'agent'`. The account pin (`explain(USER_ACCOUNT)` reads `'agent'`) would go red under an unconditional stamp. A service account reads `'agent'` because `buildContextForUser` spreads `grants.principalKind`, which `isAgentAccountRow` (`resolve-authz-context.ts:2028`) sets from `sys_user.principal_kind`. That column offers only `human` and `agent`, so "no kind ⇒ person" is the resolver's own rule. Residual (nit): `tryFind` swallows read errors. If the resolver's `sys_user` read failed while the existence read succeeded, an account would be explained as `'human'`. In that case enforcement would also have resolved it as a person, so the label agrees with the verdict, but it is inferred rather than read from the row the branch already holds.
  - (d) Holds structurally. `runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts:1330` passes `session: engineCtx?.session` through whole, and `cli/test/lowered-body-face-enumeration.test.ts:281` pins `session` as passthrough. No test in this PR reads the key from inside a sandboxed body (nit).
  - (e) No masking found. The objectql, plugin-audit and plugin-security pins build envelopes through `assembleExecutionContext` / `assembleExecutionContextOrGuest`. The explain rig adds a real `sys_user` row with `principal_kind: 'agent'` and a membership row. Each negative pin (no default, no session from a kind alone, no metadata or kind column for an account) is matched by a reported red ablation (A1–A3, B1–B3, C1, C2).
  - (f) Holds. `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` is in the changeset.
- Nits, none blocking:
  - (n1) The explain stamp could be read from the `readSysUserRow` result through `isAgentAccountRow` instead of being inferred from the resolver's silence. See the residual under (c).
  - (n2) There is no sandboxed-body pin for the key.
  - (n3) The five-value enum literal is now written out in four places in spec, with no shared schema or drift guard. This follows existing practice.

### ② Semver level

- The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. Under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the level follows Metadata-protocol, and `added` (a new key that hook bodies read) owes `minor`. The precedents #30800 (`provenance.impersonatedBy`) and #26831 (`session.locale`) were graded the same way.
- The changeset `.changeset/31740-principal-kind-reaches-hooks-and-explain.md` sets `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: patch` and `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`. These are exactly the packages with production changes (spec 33 lines, objectql 6, plugin-security 7). `plugin-audit` changes only tests and correctly has no entry. `content/docs` is not a package. `Check Changeset` is green.
- The `Skills-docs:` line is present in the PR body: the follow-up is owed, and triage files the `domain:skills` child (rule 5, per triage 6730398547).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Console** `AccessExplainPanel.tsx` does not render `principal.principalKind`. This goes to the UI lane, is the seat-named follow-up (dev open_question, option A), and is not built here. It is still to be filed.
- **Skills child.** No `domain:skills` child card exists yet (searched at review time). Triage owes it now that the card is claimed. It should also correct `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx:118`, which still teaches `provenance.performedByClientId` as the agent signal.
- **Action-body `ctx.session`** (`runtime/src/action-execution.ts` `buildActionSession`) does not carry the key. This is a separate object that no contract declares the key on. The dev noted it as out of scope and no defect is filed; that is correct.
- **`'service'` and `'system'`** have no producer today. The key copies the envelope verbatim, which is the ruled behavior.
- **`protocol:data` label.** The labeler attaches it for any `packages/spec/src/data/**` change. The seat ruled it expected and not a stop (amendment 6755781269, precedent #30800).
- **Deviations** (work done in the card thread's checkout rather than a separate worktree, the C2 ablation marker stripped by the bundler, no per-package lint script) leave the contract unchanged.
- **CI at review time.** 45 check-runs on the head: 25 completed, all success or skipped, with none failed; 20 still in progress (Build Core/Docs/UI Deps, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Type Check workspace / debt ledger / consumer gates, four Lint jobs, Live E2E UI). This verdict covers the contract only and assumes those runs land green.

**VERDICT: PASS**
